description: Owner staking policy. 1 unit = $75 fixed. Permitted stakes are whole units from 1U to 5U ($75 to $375). A game may receive zero bets and nothing obliges a minimum number of bets. Limits are counts of units (dollars follow from the fixed unit); bankroll-fraction guards apply only when a bankroll snapshot is supplied. Authoritative explanation: docs/NFL_OPERATING_POLICY.md.
rationale: The owner's stated preferences replace the PILOT settings (0.5% of bankroll per unit, 2U per position). The aggregate exposure, correlation-group and slate limits are KEPT and re-expressed in the owner's units so that a larger permitted single stake cannot silently loosen portfolio protection: they scale with the 2.5x increase in the maximum single stake (2U -> 5U) only as far as the 2026 ledger shows the desk actually operates (see docs/research/ACTUAL_WAGER_DIAGNOSIS_2026-10-25.md). Sizing remains flat in units with evidence-tier caps (nfl_edge/handicap/staking.py); it is NOT Kelly and NOT proportional to model-market disagreement, because no model in this repository has earned that authority (docs/PRODUCTION_ELIGIBILITY.md).
notes: unit_fraction_of_bankroll is retained only as the fallback for a policy file that sets no fixed unit; with fixed_unit_dollars present it is not read.

max_exposure_per_correlation_group_units (6) is deliberately TIGHTER than the per-game cap (8): correlated positions in one game are one bet wearing several tickets, and combined exposure is assessed per group.

The slate cap is the MORE BINDING of the unit count (25U = $1,875) and, when a bankroll is supplied, the bankroll fraction (10%). bankroll_max_stake_fraction (3%) likewise only binds when a bankroll is supplied; without one the report states 'NOT_EVALUATED' rather than assuming a bankroll.

Grade caps are ceilings, not targets. The evidence-tier ladder in nfl_edge/handicap/staking.py decides which tier a candidate actually reaches, and 4U-5U need evidence no model in this repository currently has.
Exposure is measured in dollars staked, which for a Kalshi long is the maximum loss.
